mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return exceeds 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero during triggered periods at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which compresses earnings for cyclically sensitive sectors and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and accelerating inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during co-occurrence of both triggers at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1,000 units for four consecutive months signals a deepening housing market downturn, which negatively impacts construction-related equities and drags on overall market returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2% in the same month indicates a statistical artifact or data inconsistency, which historically has coincided with market uncertainty and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.2% AND UNRATE > 0.2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered months at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1% for three consecutive quarters signals economic stagnation, which depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero during triggered periods at 90% confidence.
